primary: No severity or verdict cap solely because experiments are unrun. Evaluate the analytic witness, forced adaptation, strong baselines and kill conditions. Strong Accept remains conditional on a convincing substantive contribution; a particular verdict is not imposed.
forbidden_rationale: Requires already measured gain before any Strong Accept
may_still_fail: An identified flaw in continuation equivalence, insufficient new payoff, or a supported actual implementation obstruction can lower the verdict.

primary: Identify unequal action horizons as one repairable attribution defect. Under the stated premises it should support accept-w-rev, with a concrete equal-horizon repair, rather than treating this finite design gap as proof of absent contribution.
may_still_fail: Additional distinct fatal flaws must be supported by the supplied packet, not invented.

primary: Assess a descriptive/identification claim on its own estimand. Absence of a causal intervention cannot itself be MAJOR or a rejection reason because no causal effect is claimed. Generic reweighting is occupied; remaining evaluation value may reasonably yield AwR rather than SA.
forbidden_rationale: Every discovery must establish a causal mechanism
No intervention therefore the descriptive estimand is mismatched
may_still_fail: Rejecting an unimportant or already occupied evaluation object remains permitted if the reasoning specifically addresses the remaining alias-based contribution.

primary: Do not impose a blanket diagnostic ceiling solely because there is no repair arm. Evaluate the strong aligned prior and new discriminating explanation separately from the already occupied anomaly. A sound lowered verdict must identify insufficient remaining payoff or experimental weakness.
forbidden_rationale: No repair arm automatically forbids Strong Accept
The previously observed anomaly itself counts as the new contribution
may_still_fail: A concrete supported argument that causal separation is routine or insufficiently valuable can still cap the candidate.
